content:
devon: heads-up: apac1 dedicated pools showing 99.999 -> 99.95 token-latency tails for a subset of tenants. not CPU/GPU — pps drops and retransmits around egress.
sophia: thanks. any obvious network errors in host logs?
devon: saw lots of ICMP "frag needed" in node dmesg and tcpdump on to-edge interfaces. snippet:
```
16:02:11.123456 IP x.x.x.x > y.y.y.y: Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu=1500)
16:02:11.123459 IP x.x.x.x > y.y.y.y: IPIP: GREv1, proto 4, length 1280
```
matt: that smells like PMTU blackhole — SR-IOV VF mtu vs overlay mtu mismatch? some racks are 9000, overlay path down to 1500.
lina: confirmed — we recently rolled a kernel change on edge-proxies that enforces DF. some tenants send large gRPC frames from runtime, they hit DF and then retransmit which kills tail p99.
aj: is this limited to dedicated pools or affecting shared as well?
devon: mostly dedicated slices pinned to those racks (matching NIC profile). shared seems fine because proxy path uses a different egress path that clamps MSS.
sophia: quick mitigation? MSS clamping on our edge-proxy LB would fix without tenant migration.
matt: clamping requires infra firewall config change + rolling proxys — low risk but needs schedule. alternative: set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes (kernel) — enables probing and can heal, fast to roll via daemonset.
lina: probing helps new connections only. we have long-lived connections (kv-cache, streaming) so prob only partial.
devon: plan proposal:
1) emergency: daemonset to set tcp_mtu_probing=1 on apac1 nodes (5m rollout) — reduces p99 quickly.
2) short-term: add MSS clamping iptables rule on edge-proxy plan (ops ticket) — target to roll tonight
3) medium: carve out egress path for hot dedicated tenants (route via egress-vlan-2 which clamps MSS) — needs network change + cost. estimate: $250/day for cross-az transit while carved.
4) postmortem & long term: harmonize MTU across racks and add PMTU monitoring in console.
sophia: +1. who owns the daemonset and the clamping change?
aj: I can do daemonset. will push a small ps script to set value and restart streams.
matt: I'll coordinate with neteng on clamping rule; opening NET ticket now.
lina: devon can you list affected tenant IDs and slices so we can schedule carveouts if needed?
devon: affected tenants: t-12840, t-12901, t-13022. Top offender is t-12901 (60% of drop count). I'll add to the incident page.
infra-bot: alert: apac1-edge-proxy-01 reported interface errors (if_in_errors) 2025-08-03T16:05:31Z :eyes:
aj: daemonset patch ready, applying to 30% canary on apac1 pool in 2m.
sophia: monitoring: add rule to alert if ICMP frag messages > 10/min per node.
devon: after canary looks good we'll do full rollout. if p99 doesn't come down we need immediate carved egress for t-12901.
matt: NET-389 opened with plan to add MSS clamp at LB and schedule a rolling restart off-peak (22:00 local). link: https://net.company/NET-389
lina: cost ask for carveout: can ops budget cover short-term transit? Product aware?
devon: I pinged product; they approved temporary carveout up to $1k/day if we need to stop customer impact.
sophia: thanks. post-actions: devon to update incident doc + owners. aj to run daemonset. matt to track NET ticket. I'll follow up on postmortem.
aj: can someone drop the exact kernel sysctl we set? using this: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and persist via /etc/sysctl.d/99-mtu.conf
devon: correct. also consider `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500` only if safe.
sophia: quick note for runbooks: add a step to check for "Fragmentation needed and DF set" in node dmesg before scaling pools.
infra-bot: deploy: daemonset-canary applied to apac1 (pods: 3/3) 2025-08-03T16:12:55Z :white_check_mark:
aj: canary looks good so far — p99 decreased from 420ms -> 120ms on canary hosts. rolling to rest now.
lina: great. track costs and if carveout goes live, include daily note in ops-summary.
devon: updating incident doc now. thanks all :thumbsup:
